sources.name: Time Out London - The best hotels in Bloomsbury

quotes.The Bloomsbury Hotel: If you're looking to really immerse yourself in the refined Bloomsbury experience, then this upscale pad might be just the thing - 153 rooms blending luxurious textiles and classic British furniture.
quotes.Generator London: Located in an old police station towards the King's Cross end of Bloomsbury, a good option for those on handcuffed budgets - colourful dorms from £19 a night, private rooms around £70.
quotes.The Hoxton Holborn: Located on the border of Bloomsbury and Holborn... just a short stroll from the tranquility of Bloomsbury, the British Museum and the shops of Covent Garden.
quotes.Mentone Hotel: This family-owned Bloomsbury B&B, located between St Pancras International and the British Museum, is set in three Grade II-listed townhouses on a classic Georgian crescent.
quotes.Imperial Hotel: Overlooking the green walkways of Russell Square... one of the few three-star hotels in an area where four-stars and hostels dominate.
quotes.The Harrison: This lively gastropub with rooms on a residential Bloomsbury street that's less than ten minutes from King's Cross station - a good antidote to the large chains.

sources.name: EuroCheapo - Cheap hotels in Bloomsbury, London

quotes.YMCA Indian Student Hostel: Ranked #1 of 10 own-reviewed budget picks. 41 Fitzroy Square.
quotes.Tavistock Hotel: Ranked #10 of 10, part of the Imperial London Hotels group on Tavistock Square.

sources.note: Own-reviewed, ranked 1-10, schema.org-marked addresses - a specialist budget-hotel review site, not a farm. Bloomsbury scope confirmed by data-places-query on every result.

sources.name: Reddit r/uktravel - "Staying Bloomsbury"

quotes.Mercure London Bloomsbury: MaudeBea: 'I'm planning on staying at the Mercure London Bloomsbury. It seems alright from what I've looked at.'

sources.communityNote: 30-comment thread, mixed area chatter rather than a single hotel recommendation. Recurring theme worth recording even though it names no second hotel: 'That whole Bloomsbury area is either 5star swanky hotels, or shitholes that misrepresent their location' (milly_nz, score 3) and 'a fair number of really really dire hotels around there' (harpistic) - i.e. sources agree the area is good but individual small hotels vary sharply, which argues for sticking to well-attested names rather than the full B&B strip.

sources.name: Reddit r/travel - "Bloomsbury or Shoreditch for first time stay in London?"

quotes.The Bloomsbury Hotel: genius4evil1: 'We just stayed at the Bloomsbury in August and the location is superior to Shoreditch. The stay was TERRIFIC especially the breakfast.'

sources.communityNote: 24-comment thread comparing Bloomsbury to Shoreditch for a family trip; near-unanimous for Bloomsbury as calmer, safer and more central for a first visit (emaddxx score 15, FelisCantabrigiensis score 13, Howtothinkofaname score 26, McCretin score 9).

declined.name: taketravelinfo.com - Where To Stay In Bloomsbury London
declined.reason: Same domain also publishes 'Best Cordless Drills of 2026: Tested and Reviewed', 'Best Climbing Sticks: Tested and Reviewed' and 'Best Coolers Head to Head' as its other recent posts - a gear-review content mill that also runs a travel vertical, not a travel blogger. Byline 'Daniel Globe' has no visible archive of uneven, dated travel posts. Matches hotel-corpus.md trap 2/4 (grid coverage, no real archive).

declined.name: eurovistatrips.com - Which London Hotels Are Near the British Museum?
declined.reason: Desk byline ('Eurovistatrips Staff'), and the page is built from the same generic template on every pass: 'Why Stay Near X', star-rated price-tier headings, 'Checklist: What to Consider', 'Comparison Table: Quick Overview', 'Common Mistakes to Avoid', and a generic FAQ block ('Do hotels near the British Museum offer parking?'). Matches the AI-SEO-farm signals in hotel-corpus.md almost point for point.

declined.name: YouTube - TravelSpotter, "Best Hotels In Bloomsbury, England - Top 5 Picks For Any Budget"
declined.reason: Every hotel link in the description routes through go.skimresources.com affiliate cloaking (Agoda/Trip.com/Trivago/Tripadvisor) rather than the hotels themselves, the sign-off ('All the best hotels mentioned in this video were hand-picked by me and researched thoroughly') reads as boilerplate rather than a real visit, and one entry is captioned 'The Gyle' while its own Booking.com link path reads '/hotel/gb/mont...' - almost certainly a garbled Montague on the Gardens, i.e. the video's own labels do not reliably match its own links. Not used as evidence; the other four names it carries (Kimpton Fitzroy London, The Bloomsbury Hotel, Staunton Hotel, a Radisson Blu Hotel) are all independently attested elsewhere in this file.

declined.name: YouTube - "UK Hotel Gems" and "UK Hotel Discoveries", both titled "The Bloomsbury Hotel | London, United Kingdom | Hotel Review"
declined.reason: Identical title format, sub-200 view counts, 1-3 minute runtime and a description opening 'Booking details:' on both channels - reads as the same faceless-review-mill format run under two channel names rather than two independent creators. Not counted.

declined.name: YouTube - TripHunter, single-hotel review videos
declined.reason: Fixed template ('Should You Stay Here?' / 'The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly') with a 'Booking Price: booking.com' link in every description, and its own subreddit r/thetriphunter has 28 subscribers. Reads as an affiliate content mill rather than an independent voice.

videoGap: No independently-verified tier-D (video) source for Bloomsbury hotels specifically was found on 15 Sep 2026 - every candidate that named Bloomsbury hotels by title showed content-mill signals (see declined, above). Tier E (Reddit, x2 threads) and tiers B/C (x6 usable domains) meet the source-mix floor without it; run node scripts/audit-source-mix.mjs hotels-bloomsbury to confirm, and revisit video if a cleaner creator turns up.
